analysis.evidence: The next verb, וַיָּבֹאוּ, gives their arrival at En-mishpat (Kadesh). The marked verb describes the preceding change of direction.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine plural, continuing the account of the kings’ movements.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68613:23, 68383:24.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol. The י־ prefix and ־וּ ending mark the third person masculine plural, referring to Abram and his party.

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּבֹאוּ אֶל עֵין מִשְׁפָּט, “they came to En-mishpat,” אֶל introduces the destination, which the verse identifies as Kadesh.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶל marks עֵין מִשְׁפָּט as the destination, and הִוא קָדֵשׁ identifies it as Kadesh. The proper-name tag fits the whole name, “Spring of Judgment.” Within that name, עֵין means “spring of.”
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular construct noun. עֵין is the construct form of עַיִן and takes מִשְׁפָּט as its complement.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68627:3, 68626:14, 68622:10, 68108:6, 67330:14, 66582:2, 66324:6, 66316:6.
analysis.morphology: Independent third-person feminine singular pronoun, written הִוא and read הִיא.

analysis.evidence: The travelers come to עֵין מִשְׁפָּט (En-mishpat). The phrase הִוא קָדֵשׁ (“that is Kadesh”) gives another name for the same destination.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Kadesh, the place also called En-mishpat

analysis.evidence: The kings return and reach Kadesh. The two אֶת phrases identify the targets of their attack as the whole territory of the Amalekites and the Amorites living at Hazazon-tamar. These direct objects support the military sense of נָכָה.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Hiphil wayyiqtol. The י־ prefix and ־וּ ending mark the third person masculine plural.
